purpose: Prospective re-adjudication of Kwajalein/Roi-Namur ground reduction after the v047-v048 integrated Japanese land+vehicle audit. Does not reroll the locked 6-Feb D-Day geography or the held first-day casualty band.

inherit_locked.state_6Feb_1800: US beachheads sustainable; Roi largely overrun; Namur and Kwajalein still fighting; no Japanese mechanism to eject landing force.

historical_sanity_anchors.southern_japanese_personnel: about 5,000 total; official Army estimate 1,820 combat effective, 865+ partially effective, 1,830 ineffective
historical_sanity_anchors.northern_japanese_personnel: 3,563 postbattle actual total; best official estimate 345 combat effective Guard Force, 2,150 air personnel partially effective, 357 labor ineffective, ~700 miscellaneous mostly ineffective
historical_sanity_anchors.historical_US_south_first_night: six infantry battalions, 44 medium tanks, 18 light tanks, five SP 75mm, two platoons 4.2-inch mortars ashore
historical_sanity_anchors.historical_US_losses: southern operation 142 KIA, 845 WIA, 2 MIA; northern operation 737 casualties, 190 killed/died of wounds
historical_sanity_anchors.historical_timing: Namur organized resistance ended on D+1 afternoon; Kwajalein declared secure on D+3 afternoon.

Japan_Namur.Type94_tankette_physical: minimum 1 confirmed by postbattle USMC recovery/memoir
Japan_Namur.role_if_high_case: mobile/static machine-gun firepoint only; no meaningful anti-M4 capability
Japan_Namur.repair_reappearance: none after capture/abandonment or if workshop/recovery access is lost

Japan_other_main_islands.note: No traced dated OOB supports a Japanese tank platoon on Kwajalein or Roi-Namur. Tank ditches do not imply tank units.

US_Kwajalein.interpretation: Difference from historical anchor is unloading/serviceability friction only. LST-224 cargo is not invented and no tank company is deleted by fiat.

US_Roi_Namur.state: medium-tank company support remains available from Roi; Namur light tanks remain useful but terrain/bogging and resupply reduce tempo
US_Roi_Namur.effect: Shermans are decisive against surviving fixed positions once routes are cleared; Japanese tankette cannot duel them.

branch_japanese_ground_effects_loaded: warning removes historical strategic surprise and permits sector assignment before bombardment
lagoon-side defense emphasis and anti-LVT choke-point preparation where time/material allow
command succession and local reserve plans improve post-bombardment coherence
registered mortar/artillery lanes become useful if observation/wire/radio survive
distributed ammunition/water/comms and smaller protected magazines reduce single-hit chain failures
earth/timber protection and crew shelter completion improve locally, but no Tarawa/Iwo-Jima depth is created
airmen/technicians may execute assigned static/local tasks, but are not converted into trained infantry and weapon counts do not increase

adjudication.Roi: mopping only; no coherent Japanese counterattack above small isolated groups
adjudication.Namur: surviving Guard/air personnel use prepared sectors and local infiltration more coherently than history; no beachhead ejection
adjudication.Kwajalein: principal Japanese effort is night infiltration/local counterattack against forward battalions and artillery/road nodes; temporary 50-150m local penetrations possible, but US illumination/artillery/tanks prevent operational breakthrough
adjudication.assessment: Branch effect is visible mainly as extra close combat and delayed reduction, not recapture.

adjudication.Namur: systematic tank-engineer reduction; organized resistance ends centered about 19:30, range 17:00-22:00
adjudication.Kwajalein: US attack clears/overruns most airfield sector but suffers repeated fire from bypassed shelters, mortars and debris positions; advance slower than the historical-equivalent day.

adjudication.Namur: mopping and casualty collection; northern combat power released for recovery/base work
adjudication.Kwajalein: fight shifts into northern built-up/debris zone. Tanks, engineers, flamethrowers/demolitions and artillery dominate, while distributed Japanese stores/command succession allow some bypassed positions to reappear. No rational mass banzai is centered; local counterattacks are favored.

remaining command network fragments under close tank-engineer-artillery reduction. Organized resistance is operationally broken late 9-Feb; formal secure declaration centered 10-Feb 04:00, plausible band 9-Feb 23:00 to 10-Feb 08:00.
adjudication.outlying_islets: minor mopping can continue after main-island secure declaration without altering possession.

casualty_working_result.rule: No blanket multiplier. Totals emerge from extra night/local contacts, protected-position persistence and slower final strongpoint reduction, offset by overwhelming US combined arms and lack of Japanese depth.
casualty_working_result.fatality_split: RESERVED; do not fabricate KIA/WIA/MIA split until consolidated Allied death tally.
casualty_working_result.Japan: garrison destruction/near-annihilation remains. Better preparation changes time and exchange, not evacuation or strategic survival.

operational_result.Roi_Namur: captured; Namur costs several extra hours versus historical-equivalent reduction
operational_result.Kwajalein: captured; integrated Branch defense buys roughly an extra half-night beyond historical-equivalent secure timing, not another multi-day battle
operational_result.why_not_more_delay: flat tiny islands, no defense-in-depth, no reinforced armor reserve, no resupply, and US has division-scale infantry plus several dozen tanks, heavy artillery, naval gunfire, CVE/air support and secure unloading.
operational_result.why_not_historical_smoothness: Branch defenders are warned, lagoon-side/local reserve plans exist, distributed stores and better comm/registered fire survive longer, and technician/air personnel are less likely to dissolve immediately.

do_not_propagate_yet: post-Flintlock Japanese fighter release to Bengal
propagation_gate.reason: Those depend on the fully closed Central-Pacific result, not merely the ground reduction.

source_notes: U.S. Army CMH, Seizure of the Gilberts and Marshalls: Japanese combat-effectiveness tables and historical loss/timing anchors.
U.S. Marine Corps histories: Roi-Namur tank employment and Namur reduction.
Robert M. Neiman and Kenneth W. Estes, Tanks on the Beaches: firsthand confirmation of one Type 94 tankette recovered relatively intact on Namur.
Branch package v048 integrated land/hardware/vehicle lineage files govern all prospective post-6-Feb-18:00 adjudication.
